newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says 7 firms to bid for Michiquillay deposit.
newsitem.headline: Peru says 7 firms to bid for Michiquillay deposit.

text.p: State miner Minero Peru has selected seven U.S., Japanese and Canadian companies to bid for the exploration concession at its Michiquillay copper-rich deposit on July 16, the official daily El Peruano said Monday.
The paper also quoted the president of Minero Peru's privatization body, Jorge Kawamura, as saying the unit's base price would be set on June 12.
The report did not name the companies and Minero Peru companies were unavailable to give details.

Reserves at the polymetallic Michiquillay deposit, in the northern department of Cajamarca, have an average copper content of 0.7 percent, between 0.1 and 0.5 grams per tonne of gold and 0.5 to 5.0 grams a tonne of silver.
Minero Peru is the country's second state mining company after Centromin. Both companies are undergoing a piecemeal privatization process.
